get-started.title: Get started
get-started.description: Install the complete Contract Check skill and begin a review with a fictional agreement.
get-started.body:
Get started

First, choose your assistant. Then bring the draft and your terms.

Pick the archive for your host, install the complete skill, and enable it. Keep the references, forms, and scripts together; uploading SKILL.md alone leaves those components out. Begin with a fictional or sanitized agreement to check your host’s behavior. No TypeSafe or Jev key is required.

Complete skill ZIP ↓Claude skill ZIP ↓Folder-based .skill ↓

Claude

  1. Download the skill

    Use the Claude skill ZIP. It contains a contract-check folder with SKILL.md, references, forms, and the Python engine.

  2. Add and enable it

    Upload the ZIP through Claude’s custom Skills interface. For Claude Code, extract contract-check into ~/.claude/skills/ or the project’s .claude/skills/. Check that the host can access the bundled files and run Python; account and workspace settings can affect access.

  3. Start a review

    In a new conversation, request Contract Check and provide your agreement, role, and objective. Check that the assistant can read the references and run the bundled commands.

ChatGPT

  1. Use a skill-enabled workspace

    If your interface offers skill upload, use the direct-upload ZIP. It has SKILL.md at the archive root. Enable the skill and the file and execution tools needed by the engine.

  2. Use the plugin route when available

    The separate plugin ZIP wraps the same skill for Plugin Creator. Upload it through that plugin’s supported create or update workflow, rather than a skill-only upload field.

    Download the plugin ZIP ↓

  3. Check the host capabilities

    A plain chat without skill files or execution can support a manual discussion, but it cannot claim to have run the packaged checks. The complete package is required for the full runtime.

A first prompt

Use Contract Check to review this fictional agreement. I represent the customer and want clear payment and termination terms. Read the bundled references, identify evidence-linked findings, and ask about missing facts that would change a material recommendation. Show the choices before applying substantive edits.

What to check in the first run

  • The assistant identifies your role and objectives.
  • Findings quote the actual agreement or explain what was searched for a missing provision.
  • Material changes remain proposals until you choose.
  • The final response names the checks actually run and unresolved issues.

See the complete review sequence →

workflow.title: Review workflow
workflow.description: Understand how Contract Check maps a deal, records evidence, asks for decisions, and checks revisions.
workflow.body:
Review workflow

Keep the evidence and the decisions together.

Structure helps you follow a review. It does not make an AI’s legal conclusions correct.

  1. Map the deal and preserve the original

    Identify parties, role, purpose, price, timing, dependencies, and exit. Separate contract text, supplied instructions, inference, and unknowns. Verify extracted text and attachments before reviewing meaning.

  2. Find material issues

    Compare the draft with the stated bargain. Trace definitions, payment formulas, conditions, notice clocks, warranties, and linked remedies. Record the supporting passage or a documented absence, the consequence, and competing readings.

  3. Choose the changes

    Review the options and their tradeoffs. Adopt, retain, defer, or customize each finding. The assistant requests missing context when it would change a material recommendation and reuses answers already given.

  4. Apply a guarded plan

    Bind the plan to the current document version. Substantive changes must link to an adopted or custom finding. Keep the original and record why each operation was approved.

  5. Compare and recheck

    Inspect changed amounts, negation, permissions, conditions, definitions, references, and downstream clauses. Return clean text, a readable comparison, decisions, remaining issues, and checks actually performed.

Know the limits. The engine checks versions, record shape, quoted passages, and certain mechanical patterns. It does not verify law, resolve every reference syntax, or prove that the quoted passage supports the finding.

safety.title: Using AI carefully
safety.description: Privacy, source verification, and review limits for using Contract Check with agreements.
safety.body:
Using AI carefully

The tool organizes. You verify.

A polished revision can still miss a material term or misstate the law. Use the records to make review easier to inspect.

  1. Share only what you are authorized to share

    Review confidentiality obligations and your AI provider’s settings before uploading a real agreement. Use sanitized examples while checking a new setup. An AI conversation does not itself create an attorney-client relationship or privilege.

  2. Confirm text extraction

    Compare extracted text with the original, including exhibits, tables, signatures, footnotes, and tracked changes. The DOCX extractor reports fidelity warnings; it does not preserve every document feature.

  3. Check legal conclusions

    Identify the relevant jurisdiction and transaction. Verify consequential legal claims against current primary authority. Course notes and drafting heuristics are research prompts, not controlling law.

  4. Review every substantive revision

    Confirm that price, thresholds, dates, parties, conditions, exceptions, and remedies still reflect the bargain. An approval record proves that a choice was recorded; it does not prove that the choice was informed or correct.

What this site collects

This site has no contract-upload form, user account, or chatbot. Contract Check runs in your AI host. Hosting providers may retain basic access logs for site visits; your AI host handles the documents and conversation you give it.

When to bring in a lawyer

Get qualified advice before relying on a consequential interpretation, signing a material agreement, or changing risk and remedies you do not fully understand.

verification.title: Method and validation
verification.description: The testing scope and remaining review work behind the Contract Check development edition.
verification.body:
Method and validation

Useful checks, visible limits.

Contract Check is a development edition. The source and mechanical tests are available for inspection.

CheckWhat it establishesWhat still needs review
Package checksSKILL.md metadata, bundled files, forms, reference paths, hashes, and extracted runtime.Acceptance and behavior in each host’s live interface.
Engine testsProvenance, approvals, structural operations, choices, reports, DOCX extraction, enforcement issue handling, research scoring, and packaging on synthetic fixtures.Accuracy and completeness on real agreements.
Review-record validationCurrent version, required fields, and verbatim passage provenance.Whether the evidence supports the analysis.
Mechanical auditSelected numerical, modal, reference, and definition patterns.Semantic equivalence, all reference forms, and legal effect.

Optional prediction research

The prediction experiment is off by default and runs only on a separately provided labeled cohort with an explicit command flag and optional scikit-learn installation. It reports held-out cohort metrics and a prevalence baseline. It does not assign a probability to an individual agreement or feed its output into a revision or enforcement report. No TypeSafe or Jev key is needed.

Read the module boundary and release conditions →

Remaining release gates

  • Broader extraction and document-fidelity review.
  • Evaluation on unseen and sanitized real contracts.
  • Host-specific installation, rendering, and export checks.
  • Lawyer review and edition sign-off.
  • Observed outcomes and prospective validation before publishing an individual enforcement probability.

Sources and synthesis

The review method incorporates original prompts informed by drafting materials, course notes, exercises, and transaction examples. The textbook and uploaded source documents are not redistributed. The skill treats doctrinal summaries as prompts for independent research.

about.title: About
about.description: TopContractReview publishes Contract Check, a development tool for deliberate contract review.
about.body:
About TopContractReview

Make the review easier to follow.

TopContractReview publishes Contract Check: a reusable AI workflow and auditable engine for reviewing, organizing, and revising agreements.

A familiar design, a different task

This site follows the editorial design of TopDWI: readable pages, a visible workflow, complete downloads, and clear boundaries. Contract Check focuses on deal fidelity, contract language, and recorded decisions.

Your assistant, your review

The site distributes files. It does not operate a contract-analysis service, receive your agreements, or create an attorney-client relationship. The assistant asks for context and choices; you verify the result and seek legal advice when needed.

Current edition

Development version 0.2.4. All implemented references, forms, and engine files are included. The package makes no claim of complete textbook coverage, lawyer certification, or guaranteed host behavior.

Inspect the package →Report a problem →

forms.title: Review forms
forms.description: Four forms for intake, optional agreement structure, evidence-linked findings, and guarded revision plans.
forms.body:
Four reusable forms

Keep context, evidence, and choices on the record.

These four forms are already included in the complete skill package. Individual downloads are for inspection or reuse; they do not install the skill. Use the complete archive for installation.

01 · Context

Intake and term sheet

Map parties, objectives, economics, timing, and unresolved choices. Compare expected terms with the draft.

Download Markdown ↓
02 · Structure

Optional agreement outline

Choose relevant sections and record include, omit, or defer decisions. This is an outline, not a completed contract.

Download Markdown ↓
03 · Evidence

Review record

Link findings to current passages, consequences, uncertainty, and the decision needed.

Download JSON ↓
04 · Revision

Revision plan

Record exact before and after text, current version, finding, reason, and approval.

Download JSON ↓
The JSON forms contain placeholders and are intentionally incomplete. Populate them from the current project. Approval starts as false. Generate decision cards and the choices record from the actual review, then validate the completed choices.
Form fields and runtime commands →Download everything ↓

library.title: Complete skill package
library.description: Inspect and download the complete Contract Check skill, references, forms, and Python runtime.
library.body:
The skill library

Install the package. Keep its parts together.

Download the complete archive to install Contract Check. It bundles model instructions, reference guides, review forms, and a Python engine. SKILL.md is one component of this package.

Complete skill package (.zip) ↓Claude skill ZIP ↓Folder-based .skill ↓Plugin ZIP ↓

What is inside

ComponentPurpose
SKILL.mdYAML name and description, workflow, and resource routing.
Five reference guidesReview method, transaction prompts, evidence records, runtime and forms.
Four formsIntake, agreement outline, review record, and revision plan.
Python runtimeIntake, DOCX text extraction, controlled edits, numbering, decisions, comparisons, and reports.
Manifest and host metadataBundled file hashes and skill presentation metadata.

Pick the upload format

Use the direct-upload ZIP when your interface expects SKILL.md at the archive root. The Claude ZIP and folder-based .skill contain a named contract-check skill folder. The plugin ZIP is for a plugin-package workflow. The skill contents are the same.

Full engine use requires Python execution and file access. PDF extraction, current-law research, and exports use tools supplied by the host. This is a development edition with lawyer review pending.
